name: Dark Navy
lede: Dark navy is a near-black blue, and one dictionary uses the phrase for a color it calls Nippon.

sections.title: A blue so dark it reads as black
sections.body:
Paterson's dictionary of colour lists Nippon as a dark navy blue colour [1]. The entry gives no more history, and the reason for the name is undocumented in our books. Otherwise dark navy is a descriptive label that sits on top of [[navy]], which is itself one of the darkest of the common blues.

The swatch here is almost black, with a faint blue cast: look for it in the deep corners of a coat, or a night sky, where a pure black would flatten the picture. Related colors are [[midnight-blue]], [[dark-brown]] and [[prussian-blue]].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: This swatch appears in 12 of 23,781 paintings, 0.05 per cent, rarer than 70 per cent of named colors [2]. The earliest is dated 1544, a painting by Bronzino, and the latest 1923, among 8 dated paintings [2]. The name's earliest record in our sources is 1955, so the match is a look-alike hue in an aged photograph, not proof of a particular pigment or dye [2]. The numbers are as photographed.

notes.cite: Paterson, A Dictionary of Colour, "Nippon", p. 278
